summary: Describes the standardization collaboration between 3GPP, the mobile phone standards group, and the IETF. It explains how the two organizations coordinate work where Internet protocols are used in mobile networks.

plainLanguage.summary: 3GPP and the IETF work on related technology but follow their own processes. RFC 3113 describes how they can share documents, discuss issues and find the right contacts.

subtitle: Guidelines for collaboration between 3GPP and the IETF on Internet-related specifications.

tldr.problem: 3GPP specifications use Internet technologies, while the IETF has separate working groups and procedures. The organizations need a way to share work and raise technical issues without duplicating effort.
tldr.mechanism: The memo sets collaboration principles: preserve each organization's procedures, share drafts, discuss technical work through mailing lists and use named contacts for coordination.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3113 documents the proposed working relationship. It is an Informational, non-protocol document.

today: RFC 3113 is Informational. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Purpose of the Collaboration
sections.content:
The memo sets principles for collaboration between 3GPP and the IETF. Its stated aim is timely development of technical specifications that interoperate with existing fixed and mobile Internet systems, devices and protocols.

Each organization continues to use its own rules and procedures, including those for intellectual property, specification development, approval and maintenance.
sections.plainLanguage: The two organizations want their technical work to fit together. Each keeps its own process for producing and approving specifications.

sections.title: Sharing Standards and Expertise
sections.content:
3GPP's preferred approach is to use IETF standards unchanged when feasible, and the memo says 3GPP does not intend to duplicate IETF work. If additions or changes are needed, 3GPP should raise the issue with the appropriate IETF working group or, if none fits, an Area Director.

The IETF can also draw on 3GPP's wireless expertise. The memo outlines the responsibilities of the 3GPP Technical Specification Groups, including radio access, core network, terminal and service aspects.
sections.plainLanguage: 3GPP can reuse Internet standards when they meet its needs. When they do not, it can ask the relevant IETF group to discuss the gap.

sections.title: Sharing Documents and Communicating
sections.content:
Both organizations encourage sharing draft documents of mutual interest. Their public websites provide access to documents, including IETF Internet Drafts. Contact points can help participants understand how to find and use each organization's documents.

Most technical discussion and decision-making takes place on mailing lists, so interested people are encouraged to subscribe and participate. Formal communication is also permitted when needed, with technical leaders and IETF Area Directors able to facilitate it.
sections.plainLanguage: They share draft documents and do most technical discussion by email. Leaders can arrange formal communication when a topic needs it.

sections.title: Contacts and Participation
sections.content:
3GPP establishes an IETF rapporteur function in TSG-SA as an initial contact for cooperation. The memo proposes an IAB-appointed 3GPP liaison as an IETF administrative contact when other channels do not fit. The liaison works by email and cannot make exceptions to IETF procedures.

The IETF may appoint a rapporteur to attend 3GPP technical meetings in specific cases. IETF meetings are open to interested individuals, and 3GPP partners or members may participate under existing IETF procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: Each organization identifies people who can direct questions to the right place. The liaison role does not change either organization's rules.
